description: This line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC, in percent) of six different methods—Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, IKE, and ROME—as a function of the co-occurrence number, which is plotted on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10⁰ (1) to 10³ (1000). The y-axis, labeled “ACC (%)”, ranges from 60% to 80% with tick marks at 5% intervals. Each method is represented by a distinct colored line with a unique marker: Base (black line with circle markers), MEND (brown line with diamond markers), FT (blue line with triangle markers), MEMIT (purple line with star markers), IKE (red line with triangle markers), and ROME (green line with square markers). All lines show an increasing trend as the co-occurrence number increases. The Base method starts at approximately 64% accuracy at a co-occurrence number of 1 and rises to about 71% at 1000. The MEND method begins at around 71% and reaches approximately 80% at 1000. The FT method starts at about 65% and ends at roughly 73%. The MEMIT method begins at around 70% and reaches approximately 77%. The IKE method starts at about 68% and ends at around 75%. The ROME method begins at approximately 74% and rises to about 83% at 1000.
